cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Carry This with Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to share a burden by framing participation as part of the relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've assigned us this box of letters before the removal van comes. We wrote them together; we're sorting them together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You kept them. I thought you'd want to decide.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I haven't approved making me the keeper of all ten years. You may choose what matters beside me, not leave me to choose for both of us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the box, but I can't read them today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Postponement granted. Before you take the box, set a date for us to open it together. I'm not transferring all the deciding to you either.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 assigns both the letters, A3 refuses sole responsibility and A5 grants postponement only with a shared date, using approval control to distribute emotional labor fairly in both directions.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 keeper assumption causes A3 shared authorship demand; B4 inability today causes A5 future scheduling before custody transfer.

relationship.evidence: B2 assumes a preference and B4 offers practical custody despite emotional limits, which A respects rather than rejecting.

heightening.evidence: B4 taking the box could transfer all decisions to B, so A5 conditions it on future joint reading.

specificity.evidence: A1 van/letters and A3 ten years establish a difficult shared-history task; A5 now clearly sets the date before moving, not reading before moving.
